title: locality analyse --json
description: Structural analysis by default. With --source history the document is described by analyse-history.schema.json.

syntaxErrors.description: Files whose parse reported syntax errors, so the graph may be incomplete there, each with where its first error is.

items.description: The first syntax error of one file.

kind.description: unexpected: text the grammar could not fit; missing: a token the grammar expected and did not find.

text.description: The unexpected text, up to its first line end and at most 40 characters, or the kind of the missing token.

symbols.description: Qualified names of the exported units, sorted.

consumers.description: Production files that use any of the symbols.

location.description: The folder of the file the component is in.

component.description: The scoring fields are present when the file is mixed: each component is then scored and recommended on its own.

schemaVersion.description: Also stored in reports/locality.analyse.json, which the structure plugin reads. A change to the stored document's shape bumps it.

entrySource.description: Where the entry points came from: the suite config's entryPoints, or the files nothing imports.

paths.description: Path prefixes the run was limited to.

source.description: `both` also cross-checks the import graph against co-change and lists hiddenCoupling. History alone is analyse-history.schema.json.

units.description: Units found, including the placed ones.

placed.description: Units left out of the results because they already sit beside their consumers (rule near-consumers).

omitted.description: Units left out of the results because no move of them is proposed, by reason: no usable target: <rule> (the best target is refused by a language placement rule such as a Go internal/ boundary or a package boundary, or by `target is a grouping folder`: a folder named in locality.groupingFolders for a language in locality.groupingLanguages), no single target: N folders tie (N folders at the same depth, none containing another, are equally close, so no move is proposed), folder-sized unit (more files than locality.maxMoveFiles) and target is a root folder (a unit of several files moving up to a folder shallower than locality.minTargetDepth). Each is listed in `omitted`.

blockedMoves.description: Units counted under byRecommendation.move that have a non-empty blockers list. The report lists them in its blocked table, not as moves, and they are not ready to move until the blockers are addressed.

metrics.description: Leading indicators and the gaming check, not outcomes.

totalWeightedDistance.description: Reference-weighted tree distance over every production dependency.

history.description: What the history cache gave the analysis, or null when it was off or could not give an honest answer (a shallow clone). With a weak grade, history-based fields are tentative.

hiddenCoupling.description: With `--source both`: units the import graph places well, whose co-change partners are all elsewhere and none of them imports or is imported by the unit.

historyOnly.description: With `--source both`: what the cross-check left out, or why it reported nothing.

omitted.description: Units with no proposed move, with the reason. They are not ranked; summary.omitted counts them by reason.

reason.description: The reason it is counted under in summary.omitted.

detail.description: The figures and the guideline behind the reason.

target.description: The best usable target at the time the unit was left out, for reference.

unreachable.description: Production files the virtual root cannot reach: dead code, or an entry point missing from config.

unresolved.description: Imports the resolver could not follow, by reason.

filesWithMacroCode.description: Files where a macro stands in for declarations or code, which the parser does not run the preprocessor to see. Present only when there are some.

path.description: The unit's entry file, or for a sibling-set unit its folder.

score.description: The gain; the unblocked gain for blocked units, the sum of the components' gains for splits, the fan-in for scrutinise. Compare scores only within one scoreUnit. Candidates are ordered by ranking.ratio, then by score.

scoreUnit.description: What score counts: folder hops of net distance, or consumer files for fan-in.

ranking.description: The score beside the guideline of its scoreUnit: locality.highFanIn for fan-in, locality.minDistance for the others. Candidates are sorted by its ratio, highest first.

fanInPercentile.description: The percentage of the repository's units whose fan-in is at or below this unit's. Information only: no recommendation reads it.

guidelines.description: The unit's gain beside locality.minDistance and its fan-in beside locality.highFanIn.

rule.description: The rule that fired, described by `locality explain <rule>`.

reason.description: Why the unit has this recommendation, in one sentence, with the values behind it. For a recommendation other than move it says that `locality move` needs --reason.

entries.description: Entry files of a sibling set.

files.description: Every file that moves with the unit.

tests.description: Tests that import only files of the unit and move with it.

cycle.description: The unit contains an import cycle, so it can only move whole.

location.description: The folder the unit lives in: the deepest folder holding all its files.

target.description: The folder that minimises the unit's net distance among the folders the language placement rules allow.

unusableTarget.description: Present only when a folder with a larger gain exists but a language placement rule refuses it (a Go internal/ boundary, a package boundary, a name collision). target and gain are for the best folder that can be used.

reason.description: The rule that refuses it, for example: crosses internal/.

distance.description: Folder hops from location to target.

gain.description: Net distance saved by moving to the target as things stand.

unblockedGain.description: The gain if every blocker were resolved.

ownDeps.description: Production files the unit imports from outside itself.

age.description: Days from the first appearance of the unit's entry file to HEAD's commit date. Null without history.

lastChanged.description: Latest commit date of any file of the unit.

churn.description: Lines added and deleted across the unit's files in the window.

coChange.description: How the unit changed with its consumers over the window. Null without history.

support.description: Logical changes touching the unit and the consumer.

amongConsumers.description: Median degree between pairs of consumers. Null with fewer than locality.minCoChangeChanges changes, or with more consumers than are compared.

strays.description: Files in the unit's neighbourhood that it depends on and that stay behind.

coChange.description: How the unit and the blocker changed together. Few blockerChanges means a stable dependency. Null without history.

confidence.description: Present only when the unit's result rests on C or C++ includes that found no file: one of its files has such an include, or an include elsewhere names one of its files and found none, so a dependency or a consumer may be missing. What the result says about consumers is then a lower bound.
